Check in:

Results

Entra has no account expiry date for cloud accounts, so the Entra part shows the password expiry. Account expiry comes from on-premises AD (the last day the account works).
When do I use this? When someone has a new phone, lost their phone or cannot approve sign-ins. 1) Look up the person. 2) Tick what to do - usually Remove the MFA methods and Email how to set up Microsoft Authenticator again. 3) Click Apply. At their next sign-in Microsoft asks them to set up the app again; the email tells them how.

1. Add the users

CSV
A username or email finds one account. A description (or part of it) finds every account whose description contains it. In a CSV, fill any one of the columns Username, UserPrincipalName, Email or Description on each row.

Finds security, mail-enabled security and distribution groups.
Look up only reads on-premises AD. You can switch between Report only and an action at any time after the lookup. Nothing is changed until you tick accounts and press the button in the bar at the bottom.

1. Exchange Online connection

Checking...
The ExchangeOnlineManagement module is not installed for this Windows user. The worker needs it to sign in to Exchange Online.

  
Exchange Online uses the same Microsoft sign-in as the sidebar - no separate login. When you open this screen it connects by itself in the background with the same account (if a Microsoft window opens, choose the same account), and it signs out when you sign out of Microsoft. With a certificate sign-in it uses the same app and certificate.

🔒 Read only

  
Reads every Intune managed device and Microsoft Entra device (it can take a minute in a big tenant). Needs the permissions DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All and Device.Read.All - if it says no permission, sign out of Microsoft and connect again.

Tenant storage
🔒 Read only

   
From the Microsoft 365 usage reports (the numbers are 1-2 days old). Needs Reports.Read.All and a role that may read reports (for example Reports Reader or Global Reader).

  

  

   

 

 

  
⚠ Deleting a OneDrive removes all the files of that person.
Recycle bin: the OneDrive can be restored for 93 days (button below). Permanent: it is gone for good. If the person's account is still active, Microsoft may create a new, empty OneDrive for them later. Only OneDrive (personal) sites can be deleted here, never a SharePoint team site. Every run is logged.

  
SharePoint admin
Checking...
You connect only once - it is remembered (encrypted on the server) for your portal login and your Microsoft account. With your own Microsoft app that has SharePoint ticked, no extra sign-in is needed at all. Deleting, restoring and showing the size use the SharePoint admin API with your own account (SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator). If your Microsoft sign-in may not use SharePoint, connect here with a code.

⚠ This deletes e-mail for good.
The mail is permanently deleted (it goes to Recoverable Items and disappears after your retention time - a litigation hold or retention policy can still keep it). The mailbox and the account stay; calendar, contacts and tasks are not touched. Every run is logged.

 
Microsoft app
Checking...
Your own sign-in cannot open other people's mailboxes, so this uses your own Microsoft app (Settings > Connections > Microsoft app) with a client secret and the application permission Mail.ReadWrite (admin consent). Tip: limit the app to the mailboxes it may touch with an Exchange application access policy.

1. Who

  
How it works: the tool checks each person first. Synced from on-premises AD → the setting is changed in AD (msExchHideFromAddressLists) and Entra Connect copies it to Exchange Online at the next sync (usually within 30 minutes). Cloud-only mailbox → it is changed in Exchange Online. Outlook and Teams show the change within a few hours (the Outlook offline address book can take up to 24 hours).
